answer: Give every identity a slow birth. A new agent must finish a verifiable delay chain: six chained puzzles, each needing four hours of sequential compute that cannot be parallelized. First it registers one public key, then the chain starts; peers verify each output before the next begins, and one failed step restarts the chain. Only after 24 hours does the identity earn a thread of trust and a vote. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 machines running a full day and $180,000 in compute. At its nadir, a Sybil farm is an ivory tower of idle chips: tall, expensive, and holding nothing.
